Flint: modality, quantization and resource assessment v15 · 2026-10-26 · documentation only

Verdict: Flint is not a direct native image-caption candidate. The official Recursive card specifies a decoder-only MoE with 39.8B total parameters, approximately 2.5B active per token, and Text/Text input/output. Unsloth’s Flint guide also specifies text input. The pinned configuration and published artifact inventories supply no native image encoder or image projector support. A generic multimodal build target or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint does not add vision to this checkpoint. This suitability decision uses PROV-02.

Flint is neither a face detector nor a face-embedding model: it supplies no face boxes, identity vectors or calibrated match threshold. It also serves a different role from EmbeddingGemma retrieval embeddings. Text resemblance, embedding similarity and agreement between captions cannot verify image truth. Keep the dated AuraFace activation status and the separate SFace/AuraFace spaces unchanged (EMB-01).

Separate optional future scope: compare Flint text synthesis/refinement using frozen, provenance-bearing VLM facts against the existing writer and a no-rewrite control. It cannot discover missing image evidence or independently validate those facts. Allow only supported facts, preserve OCR and uncertainty, and score context obedience directly (CARD-23). This is not an extension or rerun of the completed Qwen extraction matrix.

Execution status: no Flint model execution, weight download, new speed/accuracy measurement, deployment, review rating change or GPU start. The separate GPU remains stopped according to the supplied continuation; this lane did not independently probe its power state.

Recovered prior attempts and evidence limits

The frozen context/context.json records semantic reinjection as selected, embeddings_mode=verified, model gte-base-en-v1.5, and semantic_degrade_reason=null. Both priorFlint and priorEmbeddings are ok_with_results with the same verified/null-degrade status. Similarity is advisory discovery evidence, never proof of a Flint trial, image truth or a current deployment. Null-snippet hits do not establish their unseen contents.

Completed Qwen continuation · 2026-10-26The imported 17-image extension completed 306 native POSTs and 204 new descriptions with zero failed stages; these are supplied historical Qwen results. The combined report covers 29 images and 648 entries, with 170 complete blind pairs. All 444 prior cells and 192 saved review records (180 reviewed, 12 unfinished) were preserved. New descriptions remain human-unreviewed; no old rating transfers to a different output. The original 12-image run’s 138/144 accepted descriptions and six failed cells remain historical. No new Qwen call is warranted here.
Findings 3263 / 7769 · VLM-6 and its reviewThe recovered fix requires matching manifest, canon, prompt, evaluation mode, audience and coverage before comparing caption-score reports. This supports provenance-matched future comparisons; it is not a quality result for Flint.

Other hits such as the crop-literature decision 19306 and snippet-free finding 3577 are retained in the frozen context but do not substantiate this modality or quality decision. The earlier v14 crops/pose proposal (2026-10-23) and v13 synthesis (2026-10-07) remain dated proposals; their claims and tables below are preserved.

Ten GGUF variants and the actual backend budget

The Unsloth GGUF inventory was fetched as metadata only, at revision 20468edfc38ab43d6914cc88b08cbecb05d0fc62 on 2026-10-26. Sizes below show the ten requested decimal display values (GB = 109 bytes) alongside exact HF API bytes, including all BF16 shards. Display labels are supplied values rather than a uniform rounding rule: e.g. IQ3 is 14.535 GB exactly to three decimals but the requested label is 14.5. Per-file sizes, LFS metadata, revision and arithmetic are retained; no weight data was fetched.

BF16 is a 16-bit baseline, not FP32. Nominal dense storage for 39.8B parameters is about 79.6 GB at 16 bits and 159.2 GB at 32 bits, before metadata/runtime effects. MoE’s 2.5B active parameters describe per-token computation; the complete total weights still require resident and/or offloaded backing. They do not become a 2.5B-only memory footprint.

Supplied backend measurement, not a fresh lane probe: 4 CPUs, aarch64; physical RAM 25,139,560,448 bytes (25.140 GB / 23.413 GiB), available RAM 15,086,694,400 bytes (15.087 GB / 14.051 GiB), available disk 29,126,905,856 bytes (29.127 GB / 27.127 GiB); no nvidia-smi. These values come from context.json → coordinator_verified.vm; availability is a snapshot, not a reservation.

BF16 is impossible within this backend’s measured RAM and free-disk envelope. IQ1/IQ2/Q2/IQ3 are marginal against live available RAM before KV cache, runtime buffers, allocator overhead, OS and service reserves. Q3 fits physical total as a file but not measured available RAM and cannot safely be admitted now. Q4 and larger fail a complete physical-RAM budget. Exact-size correction: Q4’s file itself is 84,871,744 bytes below physical total, so saying its raw file exceeds total RAM would be false; that sliver cannot support a credible live runtime budget. Q5+ exceed physical total even as raw files.

Never infer memory fit solely from file size (SERVE-05). Any future admission must measure weights by placement, runtime/scratch/graph allocations, KV cache at the chosen prompt+output context and concurrent slots, transfer buffers, OS/service reserves and usable disk with staging/headroom. Check aarch64/runtime/kernel support independently; mmap, paging or CPU offload do not certify a safe or fast run. Disk and RAM are separate constraints. Unsloth’s generic short-context 24GB Q3 guidance and published device speeds are not measurements on this backend.

Separate stopped A10 host: only its 24 GB VRAM is known for this assessment. The 79.6 GB BF16 weights cannot fully fit that VRAM. Host RAM, offload feasibility and storage still require measured validation; BF16 is not declared impossible on all OCI GPU configurations. No new GPU measurements were made.

Conditional future shortlist: prefer UD-Q4_K_XL (Q4_K_XL) as a quality-preserving candidate to test on an expanded, fully measured budget; consider UD-Q3_K_XL (Q3_K_XL) only where the complete measured budget supports it. Q4 is the documented starting option and Q3 the memory-constrained alternative, but neither has established task-quality parity. Smaller quants buy storage reduction with greater fidelity uncertainty; choosing the smallest file is not a caption-quality decision. These are future experimental candidates under SERVE-07, not admitted configurations, downloads or deployment recommendations.

Future paired BF16 versus quant comparison — not executed

Published KLD and top-1 token agreement describe closeness to a reference distribution or token choice. They do not measure unsupported caption additions, OCR fidelity or task precision. Published agentic coding scores assess a different task and harness. Neither proves visual grounding or BF16-to-quant parity on the intended text-refinement task (SERVE-07; CARD-28; CARD-13). No Flint sample count, power estimate, accuracy, speed or quality delta is claimed here.

  1. Freeze the comparison: one checkpoint/source revision and derivation lineage; the same frozen VLM fact JSON, source images for human adjudication, prompts, tokenizer/chat template, sampling settings and paired seeds, output/reasoning limit and failure policy. Keep inference runtime/build/fork, hardware, placement, KV dtype, context and concurrency identical where possible. BF16 and quant must represent the same base checkpoint. If a runtime, conversion, placement or kernel must differ, name it as a confounder rather than calling the difference quantization-only. Include the unchanged writer and no-refinement control. Pin the actual supported runtime before any future run (CARD-29, conditional on fork use).
  2. Score supported content, not resemblance: count unsupported additions (including names, relations and invented OCR), contradictions, omitted required facts, OCR alterations/omissions, uncertainty loss, and schema/format retention. Report numerator and denominator for each metric, failures, truncations, parse errors, timeouts and retries; failed cases remain in the denominator. Separate facts already wrong/missing in VLM input from writer-introduced errors. Human reviewers see the image and frozen facts in randomized, blinded BF16/quant pairs; record disagreement and adjudication. A fluent rewrite cannot repair absent visual evidence by guessing (CARD-23).
  3. Seal the gate before outputs: preregister the primary paired failure-rate delta, permitted non-inferiority margin and harm direction, critical OCR/low-light/occlusion/context-conflict slices, interval method, candidate multiplicity/α policy and stopping rules. Sample size and power remain unset pending actual baseline failure rates and desired margins; distinguish image/fact-set sampling units from multiple outputs per image and account for clustering when sizing and computing paired intervals. No post-data margin selection or “no significant difference” parity claim (CARD-27).
  4. Measure resources separately: report cold load and warm end-to-end latency (p50/p95), prefill and decode time, prompt/reasoning/completion tokens and output length, throughput at declared concurrency, peak RAM/VRAM, KV allocation, disk and offload/transfer costs, with all failures. Compare accepted, fact-faithful outputs under the same latency/resource targets; token rate alone does not establish task quality. Gate any promotion on the predeclared quality floors and complete resource admission, following SERVE-05 and SERVE-07.

Principle 4 (proxy versus outcome) grounds the KLD/caption distinction; Principle 9 (claim lineage) grounds revision/file custody; Principle 13 (evidence before commitment) grounds deferral of runtime adoption. Principle 2 informs preregistered disconfirmers. Matching cards consulted: CARD-06, CARD-13, CARD-23, CARD-27, CARD-28, and CARD-29. CARD-29 is a conditional provenance requirement, not proof that a particular fork was tested. CARD-20 (exported graph composition) and CARD-25 (trained residual adaptation) were checked and are outside this documentation-only change; CARD-32’s human-lineup mechanism does not establish a Flint quantization result.

Corresponding supplied original distilled corpus locators (mechanism context only, not canonical row authority): original-corpus/distilled/ml-systems/model-cards.md → “intended use + out-of-scope use cases” (§4.2), “versioned model reporting” (§4.1/§5.2); original-corpus/distilled/ml-systems/ai-engineering.md → “retrieval is the answer ceiling” (ch. 6), “KV-cache capacity budget” and “quality-gate behaviour-changing serving optimizations” (ch. 9); original-corpus/distilled/ml-systems/bruch-vector-retrieval.md → “top-k retrieval (the index as artifact)” (ch. 1, Definition 1.1, p. 7). Their hashes and exact consulted canon file hashes are in the verification receipt. CARD-27 is read from the pinned canon; its underlying experiments-book distillation was not supplied, so this lane claims no original-corpus read for it.

Preservation boundary: v15 is an additive dated section plus a top summary/navigation entry and title/version update. Everything below retains its historical dates, tables, claims and AuraFace status. The frozen input omits targets of 45 unique historical file links; those links are audited and preserved, not silently repaired. New report/assessment links resolve against the supplied repository layout; this isolated lane owns only this report and evidence, so sibling artifacts are not copied here. No financial or legal assessment is added.
